haiku-low.q1: MySQL first: one MySQL transaction applies the change and, if dual write is on, an outbox row. After commit, Postgres gets the copy with a 300 ms timeout. Postgres errors are caught and never raised to the caller.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the existing Postgres row is missing, or its version is lower than the incoming copy's version.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance must report users_dual_write true in app_flag_value, with reporter count equal to instance count, and the replica must have applied the recorded gtid_executed G. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s.
haiku-low.q4: Backfill reads 2,000-row batches, pauses users_backfill_pause_ms between batches, and waits whenever replica lag exceeds 5 s or the lag metric is missing.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: the step 5 comparison must show zero confirmed mismatches with no relay backlog, then users_read_pg rises through 1%, 10%, 50%, 100%, holding 30 minutes each. Source-of-truth switch: 3 days at 100% reads, empty outbox, then an operator runs the switch.
haiku-low.q6: An outbox row in the source-of-truth database records the pending copy, written in the same transaction as the change. The relay drains it, re-reads the current row from the sot primary, and applies it with the version rule.
haiku-low.q7: Erasure writes a Postgres tombstone with version 2147483647, which beats any stale copy, so the version rule rejects it. In MySQL, users_erased is written in the delete transaction, and reverse upserts take a locking read of it first.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is in migration_state.backfill in Postgres. Each batch and its compare-and-set cursor advance commit in one transaction. It stops when the select returns no rows and the cursor equals the final id, or on cursor mismatch.
haiku-low.q9: The comparison job, rerun nightly, hashes rows on both sides and re-checks differences. Confirmed mismatches, excluding ids with pending outbox rows, each get a repair outbox row.
haiku-low.q10: Instances set to paused stop writing to MySQL, and the switch checks that all report paused, 5 s has passed, and the outbox is empty. If not met by T0+45, the operator sets users_sot=mysql to abort.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres's identity column assigns new ids. The sequence is set above MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT and max Postgres id plus 100,000. A rollback checks MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is above max(id) and fixes it first.
haiku-low.q12: The step 9 reverse relay copies every change and erasure to MySQL. Rollback pauses writes, drains the Postgres outbox, checks AUTO_INCREMENT, then sets sot=mysql by T0+45. The option ends at step 10, when dual write is turned off.

sonnet.q1: MySQL (sot) is written first in one transaction (plus an outbox row if dual write is on); after commit the same row snapshot is applied to Postgres with the version rule and a 300 ms timeout. A Postgres failure is caught and never raised, so the caller sees normal success; the outbox row stays for the relay.
sonnet.q2: Only if the row is missing, or the existing row's version is lower than the incoming version (users.version < EXCLUDED.version).
sonnet.q3: Dual write must be on: app_flag_value for users_dual_write shows true on every instance (checked after the 30 s refresh, repeated until it holds), and reporter count equals instance count (no old code). Then record the primary's gtid_executed as G and wait until the replica has applied G. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s after a flag change.
sonnet.q4: Reads from the replica in batches of 2000 and checks mysql_replica_lag_seconds before each batch; if above 5 s or the metric is missing, it sleeps 5 s and re-checks. It also waits users_backfill_pause_ms between batches. Only one worker runs (advisory lock), outside the web instances.
sonnet.q5: Reads: backfill done, outbox empty, and one complete comparison pass with zero confirmed mismatches and no relay backlog; then raise users_read_pg in stages (1,10,50,100%), 30+ min each while error rate, latency and comparison are healthy. Source of truth: 3+ days soak at 100% reads (any drop or mismatch resets the clock), MySQL outbox empty, all instances report paused, 5 s since last confirmation, and the 10,000 most recently updated rows match in both stores (all by T0+45).
sonnet.q6: An outbox row (user_id, op) in users_outbox, inserted in the same MySQL transaction as the change (the sot database; holds no row data). The relay worker, scanning rows older than 5 s, re-reads the current row from the sot primary and applies it to Postgres with the version rule, retrying forever with backoff and deleting the row on success.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: a deleted user is a Postgres row with same id, deleted_at set, and version 2147483647, so the version rule rejects any stale copy from dual write, backfill or repair, without locks. In MySQL a users_erased row is written in the same transaction as the delete (and reverse upserts do a locking read of users_erased).
sonnet.q8: In migration_state (name='backfill') in Postgres. The cursor is advanced by compare-and-set in the same Postgres transaction as the batch apply, so cursor and rows commit atomically; a mismatch means another worker advanced it and this one stops. It stops when the select returns no rows and the cursor equals the final id.
sonnet.q9: A full comparison worker walks ids in 10,000 chunks, hashing every column on both sides (cursor in migration_state.compare; also rerun nightly). Differing rows are re-checked against the MySQL primary and Postgres; a mismatch counts only if persistent and no pending outbox row. Counted cases: row missing/different in Postgres, non-tombstone Postgres row missing from MySQL, tombstone whose id still exists in MySQL. Each confirmed mismatch gets a repair outbox row, and the pass is not clean until a new full pass finds zero.
sonnet.q10: Set users_sot=paused first; writes get a retryable 503 once an instance refreshes (or its cache is over 40 s old). The switch continues only after every instance reports paused, 5 s have passed, the MySQL outbox is empty and recent rows match; only then set postgres, so no instance writes MySQL while others write Postgres. If the gates are not met by T0+45, set users_sot=mysql (abort); the last instance sees it by T0+75, keeping the pause under 90 s.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids from its identity sequence (GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY). Before the switch, setval is set to GREATEST(MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT counter, max(Postgres id)) + 100000, so new ids never collide with any id MySQL issued. The copy to MySQL carries the id explicitly, keeping MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT ahead. On rollback, check the MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT counter is above max(id) and fix it if not.
sonnet.q12: The relay copies every change from the Postgres outbox to MySQL with the version rule (MySQL trails by a few seconds); erasures delete the MySQL row and write users_erased in one transaction. Rollback (any time before step 10): set users_read_pg=0 if read-related, run the pause protocol in reverse (paused, all instances, Postgres outbox empty), check/fix AUTO_INCREMENT, set users_sot=mysql by T0+45 with same abort rule; forward dual write continues. The option ends at step 10, when dual write is turned off and MySQL fallback removed (a fresh reverse backfill would be needed).
